review_avatars.name: Elena Rostova
review_avatars.title: Finally, my doctor understood where it hurts!
review_avatars.review: Before PainMap I fumbled with words like 'it radiates around here somewhere'. Handing the generated PDF summary with the exact lumbar quadrant cut my appointment time in half.

review_avatars.name: Marcus Vance
review_avatars.title: Voice description feature is a lifesaver during flare-ups
review_avatars.review: When I have a blinding cluster headache, typing is agonizing. I just tap voice, say 'throbbing behind left temple with nausea', and it maps it directly with the 8/10 severity slider.

review_avatars.name: Dr. Sarah Lin, MD
review_avatars.title: Clinically informative non-diagnostic communication
review_avatars.review: The visual body map representation helps bridge patient sensation and our clinical diagnosis. The green/yellow/red triage helps patients prioritize urgent symptoms.

review_avatars.name: David Kalu
review_avatars.title: The statistics trend showed my recovery trajectory clearly
review_avatars.review: Seeing my severity drop from an average 7.2 down to 2.8 over 4 weeks gave me hope and kept me disciplined with my rehab drills.

instructions_to_main_agent: 1. Replace default splash with comprehensive multi-route app using react-router-dom.
2. Ensure Google Sign-In is prominently featured on both /login and /register with mock auth handler that auto-populates user session.

3. On /register, capture all required fields: Gmail, phone number, full name, residential address, emergency contact name & phone, password, age, blood type dropdown (A+, A-, B+, B-, O+, O-, AB+, AB-), and optional existing conditions.
4. Store registered user info and mock auth token in localStorage so user remains logged in across reloads.

5. The Dashboard must house BOTH the Pain Diary (list of recorded sessions with date, pain regions, severity badge, doctor notes) and Statistics (Recharts: weekly severity trend line, pain distribution radar or bar chart, shift diary summary).

6. Customer Reviews page must feature rich patient cards with photos, verified badges, star ratings, and an 'Add Your Review' modal form allowing logged-in patients to post reviews that persist to localStorage.

7. Diagnostics flow: Step 1 Profile (Age, Biological Sex, Activity level) -> Step 2 Interactive SVG Body Map (Front/Back toggle with clickable anatomical pain hotspots) -> Step 3 Describe Pain (Chips + Free text textarea + Speech-to-Text Voice button) + 0-10 Pain Severity Slider -> Step 4 Clinical Summary (Color-coded Green Mild / Yellow Moderate / Red Urgent with doctor talking points and PDF/print action).
8. Floating AI Help Assistant: Available on all pages as a friendly teal assistant drawer/dialogue that guides the user on what symptoms mean without giving legal medical diagnosis.
9. Theme: Implement dark mode toggle with next-themes or state-driven 'dark' class on <html> document.
10. High accessibility: Use font sizes no smaller than text-sm, clear 4.5:1 contrast, distinct tap targets min 44x44px for mobile PWA usage.
11. Every interactive item, button, input, toggle, tab must have explicit kebab-case data-testid attributes.

anti_patterns: NO dark colors used as full screen muddy gradients
NO emoji-only icons (use Lucide-react icons instead: HeartPulse, ShieldAlert, Sparkles, MessageCircle, etc.)
NO unstyled raw HTML <select> or <input type='date'>; style them cleanly with tailwind and shadcn patterns
NO transparent backgrounds on dropdowns, modals, and sticky navbars
